scenes.headline: How BrowserSkill lets an agent drive your Chrome
scenes.sub: A CLI, a daemon, an extension, and where the consent switch lives.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Atlas! BrowserSkill lets any agent with a shell drive your signed-in Chrome. Here's how, and where it asks you first.

scenes.text: Keep the consent switch in the browser, where the agent can't reach it. To click your tab, the agent must borrow it.
scenes.mark: where the agent can't reach it
scenes.say: The idea: keep the consent switch in the browser, where the agent can't reach it. And to click your tab, it must borrow it.

scenes.title: From a shell command to a click

steps.say: An agent runs a shell command. The command-line tool hands it to a local daemon over a Unix socket.
The daemon passes it to the extension, which drives Chrome in a separate Agent Window.
Your windows keep working. To touch one of your tabs, the agent must borrow it.
Whether a borrow asks you first is saved in browser storage. The agent can read it, not change it.

left.title: Before: flags
items: All on surfaces the agent controls
left.say: Before, three flags could turn confirmation off. But the agent sets its own flags.

right.title: Now: the browser decides
items: The flags only print a deprecation warning
Anything but a literal false reads as on
The prompt appears in a window you own
right.say: Now those flags only print a warning. Anything but a literal false reads as on.

items.text: Tag each tool by its effect
items.say: Every tool is tagged by its effect: a read, an input, or a mutation.
Locally, a passive read returns early, never scope-checked.
Input stays in the Agent Window, or borrows the tab, and a human confirms.

items.text: Remote: every tab needs a grant
items.say: Remotely, even a read needs a grant.

scenes.label: Commands run against a tab never borrowed
scenes.say: Against a tab it never borrowed, the article ran nineteen commands. Thirteen refused. Six answered, with no prompt.

scenes.text: A permission counts only if its switch sits on a surface the agent cannot control.
scenes.say: A permission only counts if its switch sits where the agent can't control it.

recap: CLI, daemon, extension, then the Agent Window
Consent switches live in browser storage
Input needs a borrow; local reads do not
scenes.say: To recap: consent lives in the browser, input needs a borrow, and local reads don't.
